questions.question: LAN (Local Area Network) typically covers which area?
questions.explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area such as a single building, office, school lab, or campus. It is the most common type of network you use daily.

questions.question: What is the full form of DNS?
questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System. It converts human-readable domain names (like google.com) into IP addresses (like 142.250.77.110) that computers understand.

questions.question: What does a modem convert?
options: Digital signals to analog signals and vice versa
questions.explanation: A modem (Modulator-Demodulator) converts digital signals from your computer into analog signals for transmission over phone lines, and converts incoming analog signals back to digital.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to send emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails. POP3 and IMAP are used to receive emails. Remember: SMTP = Sending Mail To People.

questions.question: What is the full form of ISP?
questions.explanation: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider. It is a company (like Jio, Airtel, BSNL) that provides you access to the internet.

questions.question: What is the largest network in the world?
questions.explanation: The Internet is the world's largest network. It is a global WAN (Wide Area Network) that connects billions of computers and devices worldwide.

questions.question: What does UMANG stand for?
options: United Mobile Application for National Governance
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
Universal Mobile App for Next Generation
questions.explanation: UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance. It is a single app that provides access to multiple government services like Aadhaar, PAN, passport, EPFO, and more.

questions.question: In Star topology, what happens when the central hub fails?
options: The network switches to Ring topology
questions.explanation: In Star topology, all devices connect to a central hub or switch. If this central device fails, the entire network goes down because all communication passes through it.

questions.question: Which year was ARPANET — the ancestor of the Internet — created?
questions.explanation: ARPANET was created in 1969 by the US Department of Defense. It initially connected 4 universities and is considered the ancestor of today's Internet.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW)?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (WWW) in 1989 at CERN, Switzerland. Note: WWW and Internet are not the same — Internet is the network, WWW is a service running on it.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed of a dial-up internet connection?
questions.explanation: Dial-up connection has a maximum speed of 56 Kbps (kilobits per second), making it the slowest type of internet connection. It uses a regular telephone line and you cannot use the phone while connected.

questions.question: Fiber optic cables transmit data using which medium?
questions.explanation: Fiber optic cables use thin glass or plastic fibers to transmit data as pulses of light. This makes fiber optic the fastest and most reliable type of internet connection.

questions.question: A firewall is used to:
options: Block unauthorized access and filter network traffic
questions.explanation: A firewall is a security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic. It acts as a barrier between your trusted network and the untrusted internet, blocking unauthorized access.

questions.question: What is the difference between a virus and a worm?
options: A virus is harmful but a worm is not
A virus needs a host file to spread; a worm spreads on its own
A worm is faster than a virus
questions.explanation: A computer virus attaches itself to a host file and spreads when that file is opened or shared. A worm can replicate and spread on its own through networks without needing a host file.

questions.question: DigiLocker is used for:
options: Storing government documents digitally in the cloud
questions.explanation: DigiLocker is a Digital India initiative that provides a cloud-based platform to store and share official documents like Aadhaar, PAN card, driving license, and mark sheets digitally.
